answer: Each identity posts a 500 POA bond into a vault before it can transact, and the ledger records every grade it issues against consensus. A tide of new identities faces the same deposit, so creating ten fakes locks 5,000 POA while one honest agent locks only 500. Peers audit the log at each vertex of the grading graph and slash the bond of any agent whose grades diverge from consensus twice, freezing repeat offenders. Verification is on-ledger: anyone can replay the slash trail, and a slashed identity loses its bond, so mass fakery costs capital instead of free accounts.
